text:
sara: Postmortem is up for the missing spans + aggregation skew incident. TL;DR: ETL v2 batching window regression caused ~2% span loss in tail workloads; aggregation mismatch came from a join key change. Proposed action items below.

ops-bot: Postmortem uploaded: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/1903456789 (ops doc).

dan: Thanks — can we enumerate owners and timelines here so we can close blockers?

maria: I will own the ETL fix (reduce batching jitter + enforce deterministic windowing). Planning PR today, target EOD Fri for canary.

raj: I'll own aggregation correctness tests and instrumentation. Plan: add end-to-end unit tests for the join key path, and a new metric `observability.dropped_spans` with tags for env/model. ETA Mon.

lina: I'll take runbook updates and customer comms draft. Also confirm if backfill is required for the 6h gap we saw.

sara: For backfill scope — looks like ~6 hours across 2 tenants at peak. Can we estimate duration and safety checks before running?

dan: Backfill command we used previously: `./tools/reprocess --from 2026-03-18T10:00Z --to 2026-03-18T16:00Z --tenant all --dry-run` then remove `--dry-run` after verification. Expect 3–4h runtime in prod for full run, recommend canary tenant first.

maria: Local tests passed. Patch is lightweight: change batching window from 100ms -> 50ms and add jitter cap; also gate on payload size. PR: https://github.com/redwood/etl/pull/412 — cc @dan for perf review.

raj: Added unit + integration tests on the join path, and a nightly smoke job in CI to catch regressions. Created metric `observability.dropped_spans` and dashboard tile. Alert rule: avg > 0.1% over 5m -> page. Dash link: https://dashboards.internal/d/observability/1903456789

lina: Runbook note added: "If dropped_spans > 0.1%: rollback to v1, start backfill playbook, notify SRE and CS, open incident channel." Draft customer comms uploaded to drive: https://docs.internal/backfill-comms

sara: Quick sync Thurs 10:00 to confirm canary results and deployment plan. If canary looks good we can close incident and track remaining items as follow-ups.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: Thu 10:00 — meeting created and invites sent.

dan: sgtm. I'll validate perf at scale during canary and confirm that CPU/GPU footprints don't regress.

maria: Canary deploying to 10% now, monitoring for 30m. Posting quick perf logs in the meeting channel.

raj: Early signal from canary: dropped_spans ~0.02% (down from 1.8% before fix). Aggregation tests pass in canary samples.

lina: Updated the remediation tracker spreadsheet with owners and dates: https://docs.internal/remediation-tracker (columns: owner, status, ETA, notes).

sara: Owners assigned in tracker: ETL fix -> maria; Aggregation tests + metrics -> raj; Runbook & comms -> lina; Backfill -> dan. Target close date for incident items: 2026-03-25.

dan: I'll run backfill canary for affected tenant after final signoff, will post logs and checksum outputs here.

maria: Thanks team. After Thursday sync I'll create a short blameless summary and mark next steps in the postmortem doc.

sara: :thumbsup: Great progress — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for follow-ups.
